candidates.title: Samudera reports stable container volumes and higher revenue per TEU

According to the company’s latest business update, average container shipping revenue increased to US$297 per TEU. This compares with US$252 per TEU in the third quarter of 2025. Samudera said average freight rates were higher year on year. However, bunker and charter hire expenses remained elevated during the quarter. The company attributed the decline to service disruptions in the Middle East, vessel downtime and scheduled drydockings. These factors affected both revenue and operating margins. The initiative forms part of CMA CGM’s efforts to expand its inland logistics network across East Africa. candidates.title: India greenlights $1bn drive to break China’s container manufacturing dominance
candidates.excerpt: India has approved a INR100bn ($1.05bn) programme to massively expand domestic shipping container manufacturing, targeting a tenfold increase in annual capacity as New Delhi seeks to challenge China’s near-monopoly over the industry. The country’s cabinet approved the Container Manufacturing Promotion Scheme yesterday, turning a proposal announced in February’s national budget into a 13-year industrial development programme. The initiative aims to increase India’s annual container manufacturing capacity from approximately 70,000 teu today to 750,000 teu, potentially establishing the country as a significant international supplier of shipping containers. Chinese manufacturers currently account for more than 95% of global dry freight container production and virtually the entire refrigerated container market. India hopes to erode that dominance through a combination of production subsidies, subsidised financing and investment in manufacturing infrastructure. The programme includes INR88.

candidates.excerpt: Silverstreak provides $20m private credit facility to Fingular Singapore-based private credit firm Silverstreak Group has provided a $20m (£15m) credit facility to fintech group Fingular to support the expansion of its lending operations in Malaysia. The facility will be used to grow Fingular’s near-prime consumer and small and medium-sized enterprise (SME) financing business, taking total funding for its Malaysian lending operations to more than $50m. Fingular offers conventional and Shariah-compliant financing products in Malaysia including consumer loans, micro-SME financing with terms of up to 14 months, and buy now, pay later (BNPL) services. Its AhaPay BNPL platform is used by more than 2,000 merchants, while its wider Malaysian financial platform has over 2.6 million registered users. candidates.title: Non-bank NAV lending margins widen despite fund finance pricing pressure
candidates.excerpt: Non-bank NAV lending margins widen despite fund finance pricing pressure Non-bank lenders are charging increasingly higher margins on complex net asset value (NAV) facilities despite wider pricing compression across the fund finance market, according to a new report from Corpay Private Markets. The fifth edition of the firm’s Lender Book Report found that average non-bank NAV lending margins widened from 756 basis points in February 2025 to 794 basis points in August 2026. By contrast, average bank NAV margins narrowed from 447 to 435 basis points over the same period. This comes as the fund finance lender base continues to diversify, with alternative credit providers accounting for around 30 per cent of lenders tracked by Corpay’s Alpha Match platform, up from roughly 25 per cent three years ago. candidates.excerpt: Police recovered approximately $54,000 in stolen Hot Wheels merchandise following a freight train burglary in Colton, California. A witness called 911 around 3 a.m. Thursday, October 22, reporting suspicious activity near railroad tracks. Officers spotted a black Chevrolet Silverado leaving the area and initiated a traffic stop. The investigation ended with one arrest and 350 boxes of toy cars in police custody. According to video released by the Colton Police Department, the caller reported people stealing merchandise near Maple Street. An officer positioned himself near Seventh Street and La Cadena Drive while monitoring the surrounding roads. Footage shows authorities following the pickup before stopping its driver. The man exited with his hands on his head, and officers took him into custody. The department confirmed the recovery in its October 22 Facebook announcement. candidates.source: Federal Register (Transportation Department, Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration)
candidates.excerpt: Hazardous Materials: Harmonization With International Standards. Transportation Department, Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration. Proposed Rule. PHMSA proposes to update the Hazardous Materials Regulations to adopt certain international regulations and standards related to proper shipping names, hazard classes, packing groups, special provisions, packaging authorizations, air transport quantity limitations, and vessel stowage requirements. These proposed amendments are intended to maintain consistency with the latest international regulations and standards, to reduce costs to entities or individuals within the United States, and to lower the cost of regulations on the U.S. economy.
